LESSON: READING 1.2.1 READING COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Reading 1.2.1 Reading comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 1.2.1 Reading comprehension. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How should we read a text to get accurate information?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. respond to direct and inferential questions from a text for comprehension
2. use the dictionary to find the meaning of vocabulary used in texts for understanding
3. appreciate indigenous home designs for indigenous knowledge acquisition

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 1.2.1 READING COMPREHENSION
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 1.2.1 Reading comprehension helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 1.2.1 READING COMPREHENSION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Respond to direct and inferential questions from a text for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to respond to direct and inferential questions from a text for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond to direct and inferential questions from a text for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 1.2.1 Reading comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond to direct and inferential questions from a text for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use the dictionary to find the meaning of vocabulary used in texts for understanding

What this means
In this part you learn to use the dictionary to find the meaning of vocabulary used in texts for understanding. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use the dictionary to find the meaning of vocabulary used in texts for understanding.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 1.2.1 Reading comprehension to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use the dictionary to find the meaning of vocabulary used in texts for understanding. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate indigenous home designs for indigenous knowledge acquisition

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate indigenous home designs for indigenous knowledge acquisition. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate indigenous home designs for indigenous knowledge acquisition.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate indigenous home designs for indigenous knowledge acquisition. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 1.2.1 Reading comprehension is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 1.2.1 Reading comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: respond to direct and inferential questions from a text for comprehension)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 1.2.1 Reading comprehension to a partner. (skill: use the dictionary to find the meaning of vocabulary used in texts for understanding)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate indigenous home designs for indigenous knowledge acquisition)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 1.2.1 Reading comprehension to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: respond to direct and inferential questions from a text for comprehension.
3. Practise this skill: use the dictionary to find the meaning of vocabulary used in texts for understanding.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate indigenous home designs for indigenous knowledge acquisition.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 1.2.1 Reading comprehension from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 1.2.1 Reading comprehension: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Reading 1.2.1 Reading comprehension?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How should we read a text to get accurate information?
2. Why is it important to showcase our indigenous homes?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 1.2.1 Reading comprehension means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: respond to direct and inferential questions from a text for comprehension.
5. Be able to: use the dictionary to find the meaning of vocabulary used in texts for understanding.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
